title: AI_LOOP_STATE.md scaffold heading no longer matches the cycle-counting regex
body:
src/afk/loop_state.ts's CYCLE_ENTRY regex (`/^### Cycle result/gm`) is the only thing countCycleEntries/completedCycleCount/totalCycleCount/rotateLoopState match against, and totalCycleCount explicitly feeds the generated-eval seed window (assessor.ts generatedEvalSeedBase) per this file's own header comment.

src/ai-loop.ts (around line 533) now writes each new cycle's scaffold heading as `## AFK Cycle ${stamp}` (a level-2 heading, literal text 'AFK Cycle'), not `### Cycle result - <slug>`. Every historical entry in AI_LOOP_STATE.md before the 2026-08-29 two-loop migration uses the old '### Cycle result - slug' heading; every scaffold generated since (e.g. the live '## AFK Cycle 2026-09-05T23-14-29-702Z' entry at the time of this filing) does not match CYCLE_ENTRY at all.

Net effect: countCycleEntries silently stops counting any cycle that only ever gets the new-format heading. If the intent is that the agent renames/prepends a proper '### Cycle result - <slug>' entry when it 'completes' the scaffold (matching the entry contract at the top of AI_LOOP_STATE.md and the loop_state.ts docstring 'A cycle scaffold sits below the rich history until its final result is prepended'), that handoff is not written down anywhere the completing agent can find deterministically, and nothing verifies it happened — a cycle that completes the scaffold in place (extends the terse Assess/Rec/Guard lines without renaming the heading or relocating it above the rich history) leaves a permanently uncounted cycle with no error.

Fix should either: (a) make ai-loop.ts emit a heading CYCLE_ENTRY actually matches (or make CYCLE_ENTRY match both forms), or (b) make the scaffold-completion step (and a test) enforce the prepend-and-rename handoff loop_state.ts's docstring describes, so a cycle cannot land without being counted. tests/unit/loop_state.test.ts and tests/regression/loop_state_rotation.test.ts already fixture the old heading and would need the same reconciliation.
